chunks: And what he narrated - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd from Abu Muhammad al-Ansari from Amr ibn Shimir from Jabir who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a midwife: Is it permissible for the newborn to marry her? He said, 'No, and not her daughter either, for she is one of his mothers.'

Because we interpret these two reports as indicating a type of dislike (karahah) if the midwife has accepted and raised the newborn. As for if she did not raise him, then there is no dislike in that at all. And that which reveals what we mentioned is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Does a midwife become a mother to the newborn for marriage purposes?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Jabir to clarify the scope of milk kinship (radhāʿ) for midwives, distinguishing between a ruling of impermissibility (haram) and mere dislike (karaha). He notes that while the hadith suggests the midwife and her daughter become 'mothers' to the child, the strict prohibition applies primarily when she has nursed and raised him; otherwise, the relationship is characterized by karaha, allowing for more flexibility in marriage. This reflects the Shia scholarly approach of reconciling apparent contradictions in hadith by contextualizing the degree of legal binding based on the extent of the nursing relationship.
